one_liner: CRM platform for managing contacts, pipelines, and sales relationships.

evidence.claim: Copper's Developer API supports two auth methods: API keys and OAuth2.0
evidence.quote: There are two ways to access the Copper Developer API: API keys and OAuth2.0. API Keys are suitable for individual users, while OAuth2.0 is the preferred approach for partner integrations.

evidence.claim: API keys are self-serve, generated inside the Copper web app settings
evidence.quote: To generate an API token, in the Copper web app go to System settings > API Keys and click the 'GENERATE API KEY' button.

evidence.claim: OAuth2.0 requires manually registering the application by contacting Copper
evidence.quote: To register your application, contact us. You will need to provide the name and purpose of your application as well as a URL to an HTTPS endpoint that will handle the secure callback.

evidence.claim: The API is RESTful with JSON responses covering most Copper resources
evidence.quote: The Copper Developer API ("Dev API") provides a RESTful interface with JSON-formatted responses to access most Copper resources.

evidence.claim: Only workspace admin users can generate API keys
evidence.quote: API Keys can be used to create, read, update, and delete data in Copper. Only Admin users are able to generate API Keys.

notes: developer.copper.co results are a different company (crypto custody platform), not the CRM; ignore them. OAuth tokens are Bearer tokens; only one scope ('developer/v1/all') is supported, granting full read/modify access. OAuth client registration is manual via contacting Copper, which adds friction for partner-style integrations, but per-user API keys are self-serve in-app. Key generation restricted to admin users per help center. Whether a free tier/trial includes API access is not covered in the supplied material, hence access=unknown; base URL previously at api.prosperworks.com (legacy rebrand).
